topics: 👻 Demons All Around — Abba Binyamin, Abaye, Rav Huna's thousand and ten thousand, and Rava's list of their effects
🕍 Where the Shekhina Rests — a synagogue, ten who pray, three who judge, two who learn, even one alone
📿 God's Tefillin — Isaiah 62:8 and the verses of Israel's praise written inside
🚶 Synagogue Manners — a fixed place like Abraham, running in but not striding out, never praying behind the synagogue
🏆 'The Reward Is For...' — running, crowding, reasoning, silence, charity, wailing, and good words
⏰ Rav Huna's Teachings — vigilance at Mincha, gladdening a groom, fear of Heaven, and greeting first

overview.title: 📖 Overview: The Shekhina in the Synagogue
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 6a–6b
overview.hebrewSource: וּמִנַּיִן לַעֲשָׂרָה שֶׁמִּתְפַּלְּלִין שֶׁשְּׁכִינָה עִמָּהֶם — שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: אֱלֹהִים נִצָּב בַּעֲדַת אֵל
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf opens with the reward for waiting for one's fellow in the synagogue, then plunges into a startling baraita of Abba Binyamin: if the eye could see, no creature could withstand the demons. Abba Binyamin's next statement — prayer is heard only in a synagogue — leads Ravin bar Rav Adda to map where the Divine Presence rests: with ten who pray, three who judge, two who learn, even one alone. The same tradition asks what is written in God's own tefillin. The second amud is a string of teachings about synagogue conduct: God asks after a regular who is missing, one should fix a place for prayer like Abraham, run to a lecture even on Shabbat, and never pray behind the synagogue with one's back to it. It closes with Rabbi Ḥelbo's chain of Rav Huna's sayings on Mincha, weddings, fear of Heaven, and greeting.

slides.title: 🕍 Where Does the Shekhina Rest?
slides.subtitle: Ravin bar Rav Adda in the name of Rabbi Yitzḥak — and why each smaller group still needs its own verse
headers: Why say it, if fewer already suffice?
rows: 'God stands in the congregation of God' (Ps. 82:1)
The Shekhina arrives before the ten; for three it comes only once they sit
'In the midst of the judges He judges' (Ps. 82:1)
You might think judgment merely keeps the peace and is not Torah — it teaches that judgment is also Torah
'Then those who feared the Lord spoke one with another... and a book of remembrance was written' (Mal. 3:16)
Two have their words written in the book of remembrance; one does not
'In every place where I cause My name to be mentioned, I will come to you and bless you' (Ex. 20:21)
Even a single learner is blessed

callout.label: Rav Ashi on 'those who think upon His name':
callout.text: One who intended to do a mitzva and was prevented by circumstances beyond his control — Scripture credits him as if he did it. And Abba Binyamin: a person's prayer is fully heard only in a synagogue — 'to hear the song and the prayer' (I Kings 8:28): in a place of song, there let prayer be.

slides.title: 📿 What Is Written in God's Tefillin?
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Avin bar Rav Adda: 'The Lord has sworn by His right hand and by the arm of His strength' (Isa. 62:8) — His right hand is Torah, the arm of His strength is tefillin

lines.speaker: R' Naḥman
lines.text: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak to Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin: these tefillin of the Master of the world — what is written in them?

lines.speaker: R' Ḥiyya
lines.text: 'Who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land' (I Chron. 17:21).

lines.speaker: R' Naḥman
lines.text: Does the Holy One really glory in the praise of Israel?

lines.speaker: R' Ḥiyya
lines.text: Yes. 'You have affirmed the Lord this day' and 'the Lord has affirmed you this day' (Deut. 26:17–18): You made Me a single entity in the world — שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ ה׳ אֶחָד — and I will make you a single entity in the world: 'Who is like Your people Israel, one nation.'

lines.speaker: Rav Aḥa
lines.text: Rav Aḥa son of Rava to Rav Ashi: fine for one compartment — what is in the other compartments of the head tefillin?

lines.speaker: Rav Ashi
lines.text: 'For who is a great nation', 'And who is a great nation' (Deut. 4:7–8), 'Happy are you, Israel' (33:29), 'Or has God attempted' (4:34), 'And to elevate you above all nations' (26:19).

lines.speaker: Rav Aḥa
lines.text: Then there are too many compartments! Rather: the two 'great nation' verses share one; 'Happy are you' and 'Who is like Your people' share one; 'Or has God attempted' is one; 'And to elevate you' is one — and on the arm, all are written together.

callout.label: Tefillin as strength:
callout.text: 'All the nations shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you, and they will fear you' (Deut. 28:10) — Rabbi Eliezer the Great: these are the tefillin of the head.

slides.title: 🙅 Praying Behind the Synagogue
slides.subtitle: Rav Huna reads Psalm 12:9 — 'The wicked walk round about, when vileness is exalted among the sons of men'

nodes.content: ❌ Rav Huna: one who prays behind the synagogue is called wicked — 'the wicked walk round about'
🔄 Abaye: only if he does not turn his face toward the synagogue; if he faces it, there is no objection
⚔️ A man prayed behind a synagogue with his back to it. Elijah, appearing as an Arab, said: 'Is this how you stand before your Master?' — drew a sword and killed him
❓ And the end of the verse — 'when vileness [kerum zulut] is exalted among the sons of men'?

columns.label: Rav Beivai's answer
columns.content: Things that stand at the height of the world (רוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם) — yet people treat them with contempt

columns.label: R' Yoḥanan & R' Elazar
columns.content: One who needs other people — his face changes like the kerum, a seabird (Rav Dimi) that shifts colors as the sun rises

columns.label: R' Ami & R' Asi
columns.content: It is as if he is judged with two judgments, fire and water — 'we came through fire and water' (Ps. 66:12)

callout.label: Result:
callout.text: Facing away from the congregation is contempt for the synagogue; the verse's second half turns to the shame of dependence on others.

slides.title: 🚶 Synagogue Habits: Praised and Faulted
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Yitzḥak, Rabbi Yoḥanan, and Rav Huna on showing up, staying put, and how to walk

boxes.title: Praised
items: A fixed place for prayer — the God of Abraham helps him; at his death they say 'Where is the humble one, the pious one, of Abraham's disciples?' Abraham 'rose early to the place where he had stood' (Gen. 19:27), and standing means prayer
Entering: it is a mitzva to run — 'let us pursue to know the Lord' (Hos. 6:3)

Rabbi Zeira: I once thought sages running to the Shabbat lecture were desecrating Shabbat — until I heard Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: always run to a matter of halakha, even on Shabbat (Hos. 11:10). Now I run too

boxes.title: Faulted
items: A regular who misses a day — God asks after him (Isa. 50:10): if he went for a mitzva, he has light; for an optional matter, no light, because he should have trusted in the name of the Lord
Rabbi Yoḥanan: when God enters a synagogue and finds no ten, He is immediately angry — 'Why, when I came, was there no one?' (Isa. 50:2)
Leaving: do not take large strides (Rav Huna; Abaye limits this to leaving)

callout.label: 'The reward for...' (אַגְרָא):
callout.text: Rabbi Zeira — the lecture: the running. Abaye — the kalla: the crowding. Rava — halakhic tradition: the reasoning. Rav Pappa — a house of mourning: the silence. Mar Zutra — a fast: the charity. Rav Sheshet — a eulogy: raising voices. Rav Ashi — a wedding: the words.

slides.title: ⏰ Rabbi Ḥelbo's Chain of Rav Huna's Sayings
slides.subtitle: Four teachings transmitted 'Rabbi Ḥelbo said that Rav Huna said'

steps.content: 1️⃣ Be vigilant in the afternoon prayer: Elijah was answered only at Mincha — 'answer me' that fire descend, 'answer me' that they not call it sorcery (I Kings 18:36–37). Rabbi Yoḥanan adds the evening prayer (Ps. 141:2); Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak adds the morning (Ps. 5:4)

2️⃣ One who enjoys a groom's feast and does not gladden him violates five voices (Jer. 33:11). Gladden him and — Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi — merit the Torah given with five voices; Rabbi Abbahu — as if he offered a thanks-offering; Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak — as if he rebuilt a ruin of Jerusalem

3️⃣ One who has fear of Heaven — his words are heeded: 'the end of the matter, all having been heard... for this is all of man' (Eccl. 12:13). Rabbi Elazar: the whole world was created only for him; Ben Azzai (or Ben Zoma): created to be his companions

4️⃣ If you know your fellow usually greets you, greet him first — 'seek peace and pursue it' (Ps. 34:15). Fail to return a greeting and you are called a robber: 'the spoils of the poor are in your houses' (Isa. 3:14)

callout.label: Objection on the five voices:
callout.text: 'All the people saw the voices' (Ex. 20:15) suggests more than five at Sinai — but those sounds came before the giving of the Torah and are not counted.

summary.principle: The Shekhina goes wherever Israel gathers — to ten, three, two, even one — and God, as it were, binds Israel's praise on His own arm; in return, Israel is asked to treat the synagogue and one another with dignity.

flowSteps.content: 👻 Abba Binyamin: if the eye could see, none could stand before the demons — a thousand on the left, ten thousand on the right (Ps. 91:7)
🕍 Prayer is heard in a synagogue → Shekhina with ten (before they arrive), three (once seated), two (book of remembrance), one (blessed)
📿 God's tefillin: 'Who is like Your people Israel, one nation' — You made Me one, I make you one

columns.content: 🚶 A fixed place like Abraham; run in, don't stride out; pray facing the synagogue
🏆 The reward is for the running, the crowding, the reasoning, the silence, the charity, the wailing, the words

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: Rav Huna — be vigilant at Mincha, gladden the groom, fear Heaven, greet first; one who ignores a greeting robs the poor

quiz.q: If the Shekhina rests even on two who study Torah, why does the Gemara need a separate verse for three who sit in judgment?
o: Because three constitute a congregation
Because judges must first immerse
Lest you think judgment merely keeps the peace and is not Torah — it teaches that judgment is also Torah
Because the Shekhina arrives before the judges do
quiz.e: The Gemara asks why three is needed after two, and answers that one might think judgment is not Torah study and does not attract the Shekhina; Ravin bar Rav Adda teaches that sitting in judgment is also Torah.

quiz.q: According to Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin, what is written in the tefillin of the Master of the world?
o: 'Hear, Israel, the Lord is our God, the Lord is One'
'Who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land'
'The Lord has sworn by His right hand'
'From His right hand, a fiery law for His people'
quiz.e: Just as Israel declares God's oneness in Shema, God declares Israel's oneness in His tefillin with I Chronicles 17:21.

quiz.q: How does Abaye qualify Rav Huna's statement that one who prays behind the synagogue is called wicked?
o: It applies only on Shabbat
It applies only if he does not turn his face toward the synagogue
It applies only when a minyan is praying inside
It applies only to one who prays aloud
quiz.e: Abaye limits the ruling to one who prays with his back to the synagogue; one who faces the synagogue while praying outside it is not faulted. The story of Elijah killing the man who did not face it reinforces the gravity.

quiz.q: Why did Rabbi Zeira change his mind about sages running to the lecture on Shabbat?
o: He learned that running is permitted only before dawn
He heard Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's teaching that one should always run to a matter of halakha, even on Shabbat
He was told that the reward for the lecture is understanding, not attendance
He saw Elijah running to the study hall
quiz.e: Rabbi Zeira initially thought the running desecrated Shabbat, but on hearing Rabbi Tanḥum citing Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi — 'they shall walk after the Lord, who will roar like a lion' — he began to run as well.

quiz.q: According to Rav Huna, what is one called who is greeted by another and does not return the greeting?
o: A robber
Wicked
A fool
One who lacks fear of Heaven
quiz.e: Rav Huna derives from 'the spoils of the poor are in your houses' (Isaiah 3:14) that withholding a greeting robs the other of the only thing a pauper has — his dignity.
